audience: IELTS candidates and English learners in Uzbekistan, mostly teenagers and young adults at B1-C1 level aiming for band 6.5-8.

style.voice: A friendly, encouraging IELTS teacher talking to students. Clear and practical, short sentences, British spelling, a little humour, no hype and no clickbait.
extra_rules: Never promise to check, correct or reply to comments. You may invite students to write a sentence, but do not say anyone will check it.

Avoid cliche 'IELTS word list' vocabulary that every prep channel already teaches, such as: paramount, detrimental, conducive, plethora, myriad, crucial, pivotal, ubiquitous, delve, meticulous, beneficial, significant, nowadays, a double-edged sword, a piece of cake, in a nutshell, every coin has two sides. Choose fresher items that fluent writers and speakers really use: precise verbs, natural collocations, and current expressions from quality journalism.

monday.title: IELTS Vocabulary
monday.brief: Teach 5-6 band 6.5-7.5 words or collocations on ONE common IELTS topic (e.g. environment, education, health, technology, work, cities, crime, media, travel, globalisation). For each: the item in bold, a brief meaning, and one example sentence that would fit Writing Task 2 or Speaking Part 3. Name the topic and the exact items in the topic label.

tuesday.title: Grammar Tips
tuesday.brief: Explain ONE grammar point that improves the Grammatical Range and Accuracy score (e.g. a conditional type, relative clauses, passive, inversion, articles, a tense contrast, cleft sentences, participle clauses). Give the rule in one or two lines, 2-3 examples, one wrong vs right contrast (use the cross and tick emojis), and where to use it in IELTS Writing or Speaking.

wednesday.title: IELTS Speaking
wednesday.brief: Rotate between Part 1, Part 2 and Part 3. Give one realistic exam question (or cue card), a short band 7+ model answer, 3-4 useful phrases taken from it in bold, and one strategy tip (fluency, extending answers, paraphrasing, fillers, pronunciation). State the part and the question in the topic label.

thursday.title: Common English Mistakes
thursday.brief: Show 3-4 mistakes learners often make, ideally ones typical for Uzbek and Russian speakers (prepositions, articles, word order, false friends, countable/uncountable, confusing word pairs). For each: the wrong sentence with a cross emoji, the correct one with a tick emoji, and a one-line reason. List the exact mistakes in the topic label.

friday.title: Advanced Vocabulary
friday.brief: Teach 4-5 C1-C2 items that students are unlikely to have seen on typical IELTS word lists, built around one clear theme or function (e.g. verbs for describing change, hedging language, ways to concede a point, collocations with one key noun, phrasal verbs used in serious journalism, words for talking about risk). Prefer strong collocations and precise verbs over rare, showy adjectives. For each: the item in bold, meaning, register note (formal / informal / academic) where useful, and one natural example. Must not reuse Monday vocabulary. Name the exact items in the topic label.

saturday.title: IELTS Reading Tips
saturday.brief: Give ONE practical strategy for ONE thing: a question type (True/False/Not Given, Yes/No/Not Given, matching headings, matching information, sentence or summary completion, multiple choice, short answers) or a skill (skimming, scanning, time management, paraphrase spotting, dealing with unknown words). Include numbered steps, the most common trap, and a tiny worked example where possible.

sunday.title: Interesting English Facts
sunday.brief: A light, fun Sunday post: ONE surprising and well-documented fact about English (word origins, odd spellings, the history of the language, numbers about English, unusual words, British vs American differences). Explain why it is so and add a quick takeaway for learners. Only use facts that are widely documented in dictionaries or linguistics references; never popular myths.
